1.1.1:
Analyze compliance with WCAG SC 1.1.1 (Non-text Content).
Test rules:
1. Image buttons must have a non-empty accessible name.
2. Images must have non-empty accessible names unless decorative (alt="", role="presentation", aria-hidden="true").
3. Accessible names must be meaningful, not just filenames or "image".
4. Object elements must have accessible names.
5. SVG elements with explicit roles must have accessible names.
6. Text alternatives must serve the equivalent purpose of the non-text content in its context (the text shown in an image of text, the key facts of a chart, the destination or action of an image inside a link or button).
7. Images hidden from assistive technology (empty alt, role="presentation"/"none", aria-hidden, CSS background images) must be purely decorative.
8. Video and audio must have a text alternative that at least provides descriptive identification of the content.
9. Characters used as pictures — look-alike letters from other scripts, ASCII art, emoticons — must have a text alternative.
1.4.1:
Analyze compliance with WCAG SC 1.4.1 (Use of Color).
Test rules:
1. Links distinguished only by color must also have another visual indicator (underline, bold, different lightness, etc.).
2. Required or error form fields identified only by color must have an additional non-color indicator (asterisk, label text, icon, etc.).
3. The selected, current or active item among peers (tabs, navigation, pagination, filter chips, segmented buttons) must be marked by more than color.
4. Charts, maps, diagrams and status icons must not convey information by color alone.
1.4.3:
Analyze compliance with WCAG SC 1.4.3 (Contrast (Minimum)).
Test rules:
1. Normal text and its background must achieve at least 4.5:1 contrast ratio.
2. Large text (≥18pt normal or ≥14pt bold) must achieve at least 3:1.
3. Text over an image, gradient or overlapping content must meet its ratio against the part of the background behind each part of the text.
2.4.4:
Analyze compliance with WCAG SC 2.4.4 (Link Purpose (In Context)).
A link passes if its purpose is clear from its accessible name OR from its surrounding context (same sentence, paragraph, list item, or table cell).
Test rules:
1. The link must have a non-empty accessible name.
2. The link in context must be descriptive (not just "click here", "read more", etc. unless context clarifies the destination).
3. Links with identical names in the same context must serve an equivalent purpose.
4. Elements that act as links (activating them navigates) without being marked up as links must also have a purpose that can be determined from their text or context.
3.3.1:
Analyze compliance with WCAG SC 3.3.1 (Error Identification).
Test rules:
1. If an input error is automatically detected, the item in error must be identified and the error described to the user in text.
4.1.2:
Analyze compliance with WCAG SC 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value).
Test rules:
1. Buttons must have non-empty accessible names.
2. Elements with aria-hidden must not receive focus.
3. Form fields must have non-empty accessible names.
4. Menu items must have non-empty accessible names.
5. Iframes must have non-empty accessible names; identical names → equivalent purpose.
6. div/span used as controls (with onclick/keydown) must have an appropriate ARIA role.
7. Custom controls must expose the states and values their role needs (checked, expanded, selected, pressed, value) and update them — and their name — when operated.
8. Accessible names must identify the component, not be placeholders ("icon", "button", "image", a file name).
